claims.claim: Reviewers describe AI traffic as unpredictable, pushy, and prone to cutting off or blocking the player.

citations.review_text: very enjoyable game, going 110mph and npc changes lane twice just to block you off

Don't expect the most amazing, life-changing experience when you get your hands on this game. It's definitely niche to a degree, I mean, you're technically roleplaying being a truck driver if you don't already have a CDL stowed around, and even if you're that much into these big, strong and hulking semi-trucks, you might find that even you may get bored on those long journeys.

With that said, it's definitely not a perfect game. I've encountered a fair amount of bugs that have damaged my truck or my cargo in some way. The AI is pushy and somewhat unpredictable (I guess that's LA for you), and worse yet, you always take the blame! Fines. FINES, EVERYWHERE. It might get frustrating.

With that also said, I still found my experience playing this game not just surprisingly fun, but also immersive. While you climb the levels and gain access to amenities to modify your truck inside and out, you get to do a wide range of deliveries while having to stay on your toes with unpredictable events. You get to enjoy a shockingly beautiful and detailed game, especially when the sun sets or the milky way paints the darkened skies.

I just know that I'll spend countless more hours building my truck company into an empire. Who knows, maybe this might be your niche, too. ^^

American Truck Simulator is one of those games that seems simple at first, but quickly becomes something you can sink hundreds of hours into. The driving is relaxing, the maps are detailed, and every trip feels different depending on the route, weather, and cargo you're hauling. There is something satisfying about building up your company, buying new trucks, and slowly expanding across the country.

The attention to detail is probably the game's biggest strength. The developers do a great job recreating locations, roads, landmarks, and the overall feeling of long-distance trucking. The sound design, truck interiors, and scenery make every drive feel immersive.

The biggest downside is that progression can feel slow. Money takes time to build up, and some areas of the game can become repetitive if you're not someone who enjoys the relaxing nature of driving. The AI traffic can also be frustrating at times.

Despite that, American Truck Simulator is one of the most relaxing and enjoyable simulators I've played. It's not about constant action, it's about enjoying the journey. If you like driving games or just want something to unwind with, it's an easy recommendation.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that purchasing map expansions via DLC is necessary to access and progress through regions of the US beyond the base game.

citations.review_text:
Where to begin? I’ve been playing this game for an incredibly long time, and over those years, I’ve enjoyed it thoroughly. The game has a lot to offer, whether it be the game and trucks you can drive and own, or the incredible support and the team that works behind the scenes to provide amazing gameplay. 
You’ll need to purchase DLC in order to progress through the rest of the US. I found that all were more than worth it as it expands gameplay, makes your trips longer and gives a diverse landscape. Not to mention, support the hard work the developers do. The pacific northwest, the southwest, the midwest, and now a bit of the South have incredibly unique feels and provide different challenges that are more than welcome. Not to mention, how relaxing and cozy the game can feel. 

I strongly recommend getting a gaming steering wheel and pedal setup as it makes the longer trips less daunting (mouse and keyboard is pretty tricky). 

Here’s to another 500 hours of joy.

American Truck Simulator is and forever will be one of my favorite games. Nothing compares to the joy you feel when you're listening to Take It Easy driving Across I-10 in Arizona, westbound for Los Angeles, or when you're listening to One of These Nights whilst the sky is pitch black over Arlington, TX. And the fact this game is only $4.99 on sale makes it honestly a steal, and it is usually on sale from what I've noticed. Now, just because the game is so cheap right off the bat doesn't mean it stays that way... The DLCs can get quite pricy, with newer states costing more than the others on sale. I'd for sure buy a bundle of states to get started, a much better approach to it than just buying individual states. You will however have to do this once you get far enough East (up to the Mississippi River border states)

I own every state (except for the new Illinois which I'll buy soon), so you can expect an experienced and knowledgeable review. With the base game, you unlock the states of California, Nevada, and Arizona. California looks considerably better than the other two do, with California having reworks over time. California is the state I have spent the most time in driving, so it's become my favorite, along with Louisiana because of bias. Anyway, Nevada and Arizona, especially Nevada, simply because of their age and limitations at the time of their making look a lot worse. This is why you'll notice if you buy DLC, the newer it is, the more visually appealing it appears. The best looking states (in my opinion) are Colorado, Montana, Idaho, Wyoming, and then going outside of the mountains, Missouri, Texas, and Arkansas are all great as well. 

Without a wheel, it won't be nearly as enjoyable, so would I recommend it to people without one? No, probably not. But if you have one, certainly play! I use a Logitech G920 Wheel, Pedals, and Shifter, and my PC is over 6 years old but this game runs considerably smooth; I've never noticed any lag whatsoever!

I LOVE ATS!…

Game was good... performance sucked.  
Dev's made the decision to go after the console market for money....
Game is a bit more optimized... now they have taken away the UI that was quick to navigate and extremely functional just to replace it with something that takes more time to use and provides less information on what everything is.  It looks like they gave a 5 year old an etch-a-sketch and said "you're now our UI designer."

And let's not leave out the developers that run the on steam forum system (discussions) that will delete negative feedback and ban you because you reported some forum trolls.

If it wasn't for the itch.io tech demo level of UI they are pushing out, excessive monetization by making everything a paid DLC (word on the street is we can look forward to paid dlc cars that can't haul cargo... in a game that revolves around hauling cargo in commercial trucks), and a lack of listening to/or wanting to see negative feedback... it would be a great game.  The current game model suggests that if they finish the full US map it'll cost you about $500 to be able drive all of them.  Base game comes with California, if you only want to buy something on the east coast... not gonna be able to drive between them unless you dump a bunch of cash.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that AI traffic drivers behave erratically and comparably to real life.

citations.review_text: if you likes long distance driving and trucks this game is the perfect one for you ( beware of idiotic ai drivers, just like real life somehow)
If you love driving trucks this is the game for you. And yes the AI traffic acts just like real life traffic. 10/10 would drive again.

I figured after 600 hours, I should finally give my opinion. This game is the best semi truck driving simulator out there. They have taken time to make the details as realistic as possible for the ratio used. The scenery is gorgeous. It's fun to see what the pedestrians are doing. And the npc drivers will definitely give you road rage! lol You have to watch out for them as if they hit you, YOU still get a ticket!

My son is a semi truck driver irl and he says this game is as close to real life as a game can get. He has played several hours as well.

If driving a semi truck appeals to you, then I hope my review helped. Why are you still reading and not driving yet?? ;)
